key_insight: Intense infrared excitation drives a Mott-like crossover in 2D (BA)₂PbI₄ from an exciton-dominated regime toward a dense electron–hole plasma, alongside a switch from saturable to reverse saturable absorption.
engineering_relevance: The switchable nonlinear optical response could support infrared all-optical devices, although photovoltaic performance is not evaluated.
method: Femtosecond Z-scan measurements with a 1030 nm pump resonant with two-photon excitonic excitation.
Intensity-dependent nonlinear absorption and refractive-index measurements.
Transient absorption spectroscopy at matching excitation intensities to probe carrier dynamics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an intensity-dependent absorption switch and a long-lived carrier population above the estimated Mott density, supporting the proposed Mott-like transition.
watch_item: The Mott density is estimated, and the abstract provides no numerical switching threshold or operational stability data.
paper_title: Intensity-driven Mott-like transition in a 2D Ruddlesden-Popper perovskite
